releases.displayName: A hotfix for The Bus is now available!

items.text: A new hotfix for The Bus is now available to address the recent increase in crashes. This is a temporary workaround while we work on a permanent solution. Please be aware that this workaround may cause instability on some systems.

We currently suspect that a Windows update or other software is causing issues with The Bus and triggering these crashes. For crashes displaying the message “Loading is stuck, flush will never finish”, our current findings point to an external cause. Since these crashes occur unexpectedly, we are currently unable to pinpoint their exact origin. We are already in contact with Epic Games and are working on a permanent solution.

Your feedback helps us assess how well the workaround is working. Please use our in-game bug reporter by pressing F1 to let us know whether the crashes persist or you encounter any other issues. Alternatively, you can contact our support team.
We hope this hotfix resolves the crashes for you. Thank you for your support and patience!

releases.displayName: What’s Next for The Bus | Development Update 10/2026

items.text: We’d like to talk with you about the future of The Bus and share what we still have planned for this year. We’re currently preparing changes to the game, new content and the way we work with our community. This post gives you an overview of what we’re working on and the new opportunities these plans will offer.

Your responses to our feedback survey help us shape these plans. They show us where you’d like to see improvements and which issues we still need to address, so we’re using that feedback to guide our planning. Thank you to everyone who shared their experiences with us!

notes.title: For the rest of the year, we have the following planned

items.text: Multiplayer improvements: We’re working to fix crashes and disconnections and improve performance.
Adding buses from Fernbus Simulator: We want to make buses from Fernbus Simulator playable in The Bus as well.

Partial and intersecting routes: We plan to expand AI bus traffic with additional routes, such as the M45 at S+U Zoologischer Garten. You won’t be able to drive these routes yourself, but you’ll encounter their buses while driving.

At the same time, we continue to improve the stability of The Bus and work on performance optimizations and bug fixes. We are also continuing to work on telemetry for consoles and a complete overhaul of the transmissions.
Further quality-of-life improvements are planned for the future, although we can’t share specific details yet. We’ve also updated our roadmap so you can keep track of our other plans.

Alongside these improvements, new content is being developed. We recently released Update 1.2, which is free for all players, and the Ebus 2.2, while further DLCs are already in development by us and other developers. The overview below gives you a look at these expansions and extends beyond our plans for this year.

All of these DLCs will be available on all platforms. Their development does not limit our ongoing work on The Bus, as we continue developing the game in parallel and collecting your feedback to fix issues and make improvements.
Route 17 will be extended by another 2.7 km to the east, though this will take a little more time. Route 17 will not be the last route added to Hamburg City.

The roads from the central bus station (ZOB) to the Herrentunnel are already in place, and areas are being developed and decorated. More objects are also being completed, with the Priwall ferry planned as a highlight.
Many of the objects are already complete, and the next developer diary will introduce Victoria Station. London is being built as individual “islands” that will later be connected.
Third-party developers are responsible for their own DLCs, so please send feedback on those expansions directly to the relevant developers.

We’d like to host more Q&A sessions so we can talk with you regularly and discuss issues early on. These sessions will give you opportunities to raise concerns and ask about topics you’d like to know more about.
We’re also continuing to follow the suggestions you share with us and other players on our Discord server. We’re interested to see what ideas you bring forward and how you discuss them.

Beyond these conversations, we want to strengthen our collaboration with you. We’re therefore completely overhauling our partner program to offer you even more attractive opportunities from 2027 to create content for our games and work with us over the long term.

We also want to showcase more of the content you create for The Bus. That’s why we’re putting a greater focus on modding, as your mods expand the game and open up new possibilities for the community. We’d especially like to thank all modders for their work and the countless hours they put into their mods. To give that work more visibility, we’ll be featuring many of your mods from the Steam Workshop on our social media channels in the near future. Giving your work more attention is the least we can do.
We’ll keep you updated on our next steps and look forward to showing you more of the upcoming content and changes for The Bus!

notes.title: What’s next for the routes, what about the console version, and what other updates are planned?

items.text: We receive many questions from the community about The Bus DLC – Hamburg City. Here you can find answers to the most important questions, along with an update on our plans for the further development of the DLC.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/435a96ba3f141a1a2720bfefe90167119aa805e9.jpg"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/ca9273bfc8791e2a0c927a89b42929fe52d823b7.jpg"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/b0a44faa23b0c6c2385383e0fff16d69cb21d87f.jpg"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/87ba6a26b2a786a7d37fe7dc7a9c20aa829e0399.jpg"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/e0cfc7b02b474d6e35cfde02d56a25a68199c00b.jpg"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/29f4c8f0af5b3b9f6d52e2338d3e06296cd1f54a.jpg"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/e4f56e66a5e633695f4aa0b93b6fbc71b877fed3.jpg"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/f73ffa9f41c6bcdabb7af9dbcc5b6e78f3f753c8.jpg"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/eb8b62c0f6fcf4caf9f79561be44ac515abb9410.jpg"]
What’s next for the routes in the DLC?
We are currently working on extending route 17, which currently runs as far as Bramfelder Dorfplatz.
The next section will run along Bramfelder Chaussee and Berner Chaussee to the bus turning loop at Karlshöhe.
The route will then be extended from Karlshöhe to its terminus at Berne underground station.
Once route 17 has been completed as far as Berne, no further route extensions are initially planned. However, we are not ruling out additional routes in the future.
There are still one or two routes that cross existing routes and could therefore fit well into the current route network.
What about new features and additions from The Bus for the Hamburg City DLC?
We are keeping an eye on new possibilities and features introduced to the main game, The Bus.
We will evaluate which of these could be usefully integrated into the Hamburg City DLC.

One example is AI bus services on additional routes that cross the existing driveable routes. Once this feature is fully available in the main game, we will evaluate and test its implementation for Hamburg City.
This could make traffic on the map even more varied and realistic.
New possibilities for Economy Mode will also be considered in the future and, where appropriate, incorporated into the DLC.
Are the updates also planned for the console version?
Yes. The free updates released for the PC version will also be implemented for the console version, making them available to all players.

For the initial console release, the different development versions first had to be brought into line. For future updates, this should significantly reduce the time between the PC and console releases.
Will there be Hamburg buses in the future?
The vehicle editor makes it possible to develop new bus models for The Bus.
However, developing such a vehicle is an extensive process and therefore takes time.
Several bus models are already in development. These include vehicles that are currently in service in Hamburg or have operated there in the past.
More information will follow at a later date.
Future bus DLCs are planned for PC, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.
For selected bus models, we would also like to offer suitable Hamburg repaints.
One example is the new Ebus 2.2. Although the real vehicle is not part of Hamburg’s bus fleet, the Hamburger Hochbahn repaint allows it to fit in perfectly on the Hamburg map.
It is important to note that maps and buses will continue to remain separate content.
The respective vehicles will be released as standalone DLCs and are not included in The Bus DLC – Hamburg City.
Why can’t I select a Hamburg repaint for the Ebus 2.2 directly?
PC players who have purchased the Ebus 2.2 separately can already download a Hamburg repaint via the Steam Workshop.
With an upcoming update for all platforms, the repaint will be integrated directly into the game.
It can then be easily selected via the bus configuration.
This update is planned for all platforms.
Why isn’t the Hamburg map available immediately after purchasing it on console?
The console version of The Bus requires at least version 1.2 to use DLCs.
Together with the main game update, this may require a larger amount of data to be downloaded and installed. Depending on your internet connection, this process may take some time.
You can check the current download and installation progress in your console dashboard.
If Hamburg City is not yet available after purchase, please wait until all downloads and installations have been fully completed.
Your question isn’t listed yet?
Do you have another question about The Bus DLC – Hamburg City that isn’t answered in this FAQ? Feel free to send us an email at thebus@halycon.info.
We collect your questions and regularly update this FAQ with additional answers.

releases.displayName: The Bus DLC – Hamburg City: New Video Showcases the Major May Update

items.text: With the major May update for the The Bus DLC – Hamburg City, Hamburg’s route network has been significantly expanded.
To accompany the release, a brand-new video is now available on our YouTube channel, showcasing the new content for the very first time in its final version.
While previous videos were recorded using work-in-progress builds, the new footage is based on the now officially released update version, which is available free of charge via Steam.
In the video, we take an in-depth look at the new Line 218, connecting the Rübenkamp S-Bahn station with Ellernreihe/Heukoppel and expanding the Hamburg DLC by around six additional kilometers.
The route passes through residential neighborhoods, industrial areas, and numerous recognizable landmarks in the northern part of Hamburg.
The video also features the major extension of Line 17.
Instead of terminating in Barmbek, the line now continues all the way to Bramfelder Dorfplatz.
This adds another five kilometers to the route and opens up additional parts of northeastern Hamburg.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/c71bd056dcfaaa221f1676369332858ac147c5ac.jpg"]
Also featured is the new Alsterdorf depot located at Tessenowweg, introduced with the May update.
The real-world Hochbahn depot has been recreated with great attention to detail and is considered one of Hamburg’s most modern bus depots.
The new Bramfeld Süd depot is also showcased in the video.

Created specifically for the economic mode, this depot provides plenty of space for player-owned buses and future expansions, forming the foundation for the newly available economic gameplay mode in the Hamburg DLC.

In addition, the video highlights numerous new details along the routes, including new buildings, construction zones, redesigned streets, as well as many additional objects and improvements introduced with the May update.
The major May update is now available as a free download via Steam.
With the release of this new PC version, development work on the console versions for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S is now officially underway.
If you do not want to miss any news related to The Bus and the Hamburg City DLC, be sure to follow our Facebook page, visit our website regularly, or subscribe to our Telegram channel.
That way, the latest information will reach your smartphone especially quickly through push notifications.

releases.displayName: The Bus DLC – Hamburg City: Major May Update Available Now!

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/e42d11369fc44d90a90caa3c7dfc51978cb63fc0.jpg"]
The major May update for the popular DLC Hamburg City for The Bus is now available for download via Steam.
With the new update, the map receives not only numerous optimizations and improvements, but also extensive new route sections, an additional depot, and the new bus line 218.
The new line 218 will connect the S-Bahn station Rübenkamp with Ellernreihe/Heukoppel and expands the route network by around six kilometers.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/dfb991088c1a1ef7541fbd9901a38dff202a71a8.jpg"]

The route passes through residential areas, industrial zones, and several well-known landmarks in northern Hamburg. Especially around Hebebrandstraße and Leeschenblick, challenging construction zones provide additional driving challenges and create an even more authentic representation of Hamburg’s current traffic situation.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/ee803b6e5a8f7e6096ce85532f72988721a316a6.jpg"]
In addition, line 17 has been significantly expanded.
It no longer ends at Barmbek, but now continues all the way to Bramfelder Dorfplatz. This extends the route by another five kilometers and opens up additional areas in northeastern Hamburg.
The update also introduces the real-life Alsterdorf depot on Tessenowweg into the DLC.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/600396119e964a38d2bfd6f1a1f57ac25e3a1ad4.jpg"]
This modern Hochbahn depot is considered one of the most advanced depots in Hamburg and has been recreated with great attention to detail.
For the economy mode, however, a specially created fictional depot located at Bramfelder Chaussee Süd will be used instead.

Due to its structure and limited space, the real Alsterdorf depot does not provide the necessary possibilities for economy mode and future expansions. Therefore, a new facility was created, offering enough space for player-owned buses, expansions, and upcoming features.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/eab86a41f2adf4bb5ee14575dd81ffbc15747b98.jpg"]

Visually, the DLC has also been expanded extensively. Numerous new buildings and recognizable landmarks were newly created, including the Marktplatz Galerie, the renovated former gas station, Osterkirche, the Ellernreihe police station, the S-Bahn station Rübenkamp, and many additional details along the new route sections.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/a349b3ba4ff3b06884830540d0e3ad64b30a1b85.jpg"]
Furthermore, existing sections of lines 7 and 277 have been expanded with additional houses, signs, and many new details.
Work on line 17 is continuing as well.
In the long term, the route is planned to be extended beyond Karlshöhe all the way to the final stop U-Berne.
With the May update now available for PC, development of the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S versions can begin.

However, the porting process itself and the approval of the console versions are not directly controlled by Halycon. Therefore, no specific release date can be announced at this time. The corresponding store pages are already being prepared.

items.text: The latest work-in-progress videos from recent weeks already give a good impression: the next major update for the Hamburg DLC is making strong progress and has now entered the final stages of development.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/fecd4a9d946db4a484fe18a35c6dd72ab2d5a32b.png"]
Both the new Line 218 and the first extension of Line 17 to Bramfelder Dorfplatz are largely completed and currently undergoing final polishing work.
WIP videos for all new sections have already been published on our YouTube channel, which is linked at the end of this news post.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/2f7ff2d5e05274db322be39b2bdb2b1f1df3b000.jpg"]

The upcoming May Update will also introduce the Economy Mode to the Hamburg DLC. Originally, the new Alsterdorf depot on Tessenowweg was planned as the main depot for this feature. However, during the final stages of development, it became clear that this depot could not be integrated into the Economy Mode as intended from both a technical and gameplay perspective.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/bf8bf35fc9a7011e733ec236a58e32d24ad2b024.jpg"]

The Alsterdorf depot will of course remain fully accessible and can still be used freely as a starting point. For the Economy Mode itself, we will instead use an alternative location in the southern Bramfelder Chaussee area. A new depot is currently being built there, offering enough space for managing and operating your own bus fleet.

While this location represents a slight compromise in terms of authenticity, it also comes with advantages: the functional and slightly worn appearance of the Economy depot fits this new gameplay area much better than the modern Alsterdorf facility.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/f01387cf2bcc08f01871431c24aae50d2a5b85c4.jpg"]
Due to this adjustment, we need to slightly revise our original schedule.

In addition to the depot itself, the surrounding roads, terrain, and connections also need to be rebuilt and redesigned. At the same time, this new area offers additional opportunities to expand and enhance the map in a meaningful and atmospheric way.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/9dc598173dcdc04b468cb82c7a2f2db6ae2f49cc.jpg"]
Once released, the May Update — including the new Line 218, the Line 17 extension, and the Economy Mode — will be available free of charge for all owners of the Hamburg DLC.
Development of the Hamburg DLC console version will begin after the release of the update.
In addition to the YouTube channel linked below, this news post also includes several development screenshots of the Alsterdorf depot as well as the new Economy Mode depot.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/9e928081a87b06161b94f91f5aef8e714e3f71f0.jpg"]

notes.title: With the new version of the Hamburg City DLC for The Bus, new highly realistic bus repaints have been added.

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/09538cc6ca46927a8e200d6e15471d2ad82961cd.png"]

These feature current promotional designs from Hamburger Hochbahn, specifically highlighting the use of electric buses. The corresponding liveries are applied to the buses included in the DLC, creating an even more authentic cityscape.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/785c0918fffe540b4f947188b7a5fc5d21743102.jpg"]
The new version will be released ahead of the new Line 277, which will launch as a free update for all owners of the Hamburg map.
E-Buses in Hamburg’s Public Transport – Background

Hamburger Hochbahn has been consistently expanding its emission-free bus fleet for several years. The first series-production electric buses entered regular service in 2019, and since 2020 only zero-emission buses have been newly procured. The goal is to gradually convert Hamburg’s bus services entirely to alternative propulsion systems.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/8d5ba8e1c6e2b8df29024a6ff6d43679b906770c.jpg"]

To make this endeavor more visible and raise public awareness, selected vehicles are decorated with eye-catching promotional designs. These pick up on themes unique to Hamburg and play deliberately with language and familiar local motifs.
Among the slogans used are: “Ehrbus für Hamburg”, “Unsere E-Philharmonie”, and “Hamburgs neues Chancenviertel”. Some images can be seen in this news update.
These distinctive designs have since become a familiar part of Hamburg’s streetscape and underline the city’s shift toward a more climate-friendly public transport system.
Authentic Implementation In-Game

These real-world vehicle designs have now been recreated in the The Bus DLC – Hamburg City. The aim is to represent the current developments within Hamburg’s bus network as quickly and accurately as possible in the game.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/7cb6e75cc4ba68f1803e4abef39f17d42c426ad6.jpg"]

The new version also includes several minor improvements and adjustments that enhance gameplay and visual quality. For example, transparency on the roof structures at the Central Station and Barmbek Station has been optimized, and several curbs at roundabouts have been lowered slightly, allowing AI buses – especially articulated buses – to follow the route more reliably.
Work on the new Line 277 is currently ongoing. More details on this route update will follow shortly.

To stay informed about future updates, new routes, and additional content, we recommend subscribing to our Facebook page or joining our Telegram channel.

items.text: Please create backup copies of your savegame files before switching to the EA BETA Update. Savegames may not be compatible with the new version of the game.
ATTENTION: This is a BETA update. Technical problems, instability of the game as well as bugs during gameplay can be possible.
How to install the beta version of the update?
In your Library, you click with the right mouse button on the entry of the "The Bus"
In the drop-menu, you click on the entry "Properties"
In the window "The Bus - Properties" you select the tab "BETAS"
In the field "Select the beta you would like to opt into:" select the entry "beta-beta"
Now you can close the window and the beta version of the update should download right away
After downloading the update you can start The Bus via the "PLAY" button
In the main menu should now be the corresponding version number of the beta version of the update and you can test the update

Hello everyone,
Update 1.1 for The Bus is now available on PC, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

With this update, we are releasing the Economy Mode Update and expanding The Bus with new features, improvements and bug fixes. The focus is mainly on Economy Mode, additional customization options and improvements to existing systems.
On PC, you can now further customize your company in Economy Mode and use your own logos.
Repaints and components have been integrated into Economy Mode. This allows you to further customize your vehicles within your company.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/8d82b8a78d0581ccb6f4afc0c3ea8b4399330d89.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/1012528db39d70b302e516cdd29a471baf9bdecb.png"]
We have adjusted several values in Economy Mode to make progression feel more balanced.

notes.title: 🚍 Economy Mode: Vehicles visible in the depot

items.text: Your own buses are now visible in the depot. This feature was originally planned for a later update, but has already been integrated into Update 1.1.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/3679fad9f26ba4cd5e8a5a642174e0a72deed45e.gif"]
Vehicle selection has been simplified. You now only need one click to confirm that you want to use the selected bus. In addition, vehicle configurations can now be saved and loaded as presets.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/ec41e07ad79612e44a4957dfcc0218a30df5dc14.gif"]
On PC, the call function for multiplayer has been added and expands communication inside the vehicles.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38629408/6e3dbcc6802956c6312b00a2ec01a5c92640cfa6.gif"]
On PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, you can now customize your keybinds individually.
Update 1.1 also includes further bug fixes and improvements to the game world.
In addition, the update includes further optimizations intended to improve performance. The impact may vary depending on your system.
